# v57_gated_hodge_vef — the Hodge operator as a SPECTRAL CONTROLLER

> **This case is v57_gated_hodge with `modes = "vef"`.** Everything below describes the
> shared architecture; the controller here evolves the vertex, edge AND face streams with
> their own Hodge-Laplacians (L₀, L₁ = down+up, L₂ᵈᵒʷⁿ) instead of the vertex stream alone,
> and ⋆₂ is the diagonal PSD star. See `../README.md` for the diff and the wiring proof.
> Any parameter counts / metrics quoted below are v57's.


**3,023,962 parameters.** Parent: `v55`.

![architecture](architecture.png)

*Generated by `tools/make_case_arch_docs.py` — parameter counts come from building the model, hyper-parameters from this case's cfg, results from `docs/results.csv`. Re-run to refresh.*

## 1. What this case is

Both branches read the same x_v. A 2-layer PSD-Hodge branch reads the full simplicial complex and emits the per-node GATE LOGITS — it decides which spectral band serves each vertex and never predicts a field. The 8 band-specialised vanilla transformers do the fitting. In v53-v56 the gate was an MLP on the vanilla latent: a router with no geometric information deciding which *geometric* frequency band a vertex needs.

## 2. Inputs

One sample = **one whole mesh**; `batch_size = 1` is a correctness constraint, not a speed knob (attention treats all N vertices as one sequence, so two airfoils in a batch would mix).

| tensor | shape | used? |
|---|---|---|
| `x_v` | (1, N, **9**) | **yes** — the only input to the predictor |
| `x_e` | (1, E, 21) | **yes**, by the analyzer only |
| `x_f` | (1, F, 13) | no |
| `d_0` | (E, N) sparse | **yes**, by the analyzer only |
| `d_1` | (F, E) sparse | no |
| `v_idx` | (1, N, 256) | no |
| `e_idx`, `f_idx` | (1, E, 256), (1, F, 1) | no |

**The 9 vertex channels**: `pos(2) | dual_area(1) | inlet(2) | SDF(1) | wall_normals(2) | is_wall(1)`. Normalised by the training-set z-score (`runs/<case>/airfrans_norm_stats.npz`).

> Mesh usage: YES — the controller consumes x_e, x_f, d_0, d_1 and the supports; the experts see only x_v.

## 3. Architecture, stage by stage

| stage | configuration | params | share |
|---|---|--:|--:|
| Linear embed | x_v (N,9) -> (N,192) | 38,976 | 1.3% |
| 8 frequency experts + HODGE-DRIVEN gate | experts d=88; gate logits from the Hodge controller (2 PSD-Hodge layers, 64-wide support) | 1,806,120 | 59.7% |
| LayerNorm | (N,192) | 384 | 0.0% |
| FieldAttnDecoder | -> (N,4) | 903,297 | 29.9% |
| analyzer | — | 1,473 | 0.0% |
| assign | — | 72 | 0.0% |
| hodge_gate | — | 273,640 | 9.0% |
| **total** | | **3,023,962** | 100% |

**The mixture** — 8 experts, each `d_expert = 88`, 2 vanilla transformer blocks, 8 heads, FFN 352, 8 Fourier features at scale sigma_k in [1.0, 1.7, 2.8, 4.8, 8.0, 13.5, 22.6, 38.0]. Gate: per-node MLP (64 hidden) -> softmax over 8. Each expert also has a linear `band_head` used ONLY by the auxiliary loss — the prediction comes from the gated mix of REPRESENTATIONS, not from summing band predictions.

**The analyzer** (not in the prediction path) — `L_0 = *_0^-1 d_0^T *_1 d_0`, `*_1 = diag(softplus(MLP(x_e)))`, `*_0 =` learned degree. PSD by construction; the degree choice makes it the random-walk Laplacian so `lambda_max <= 2` and the smoothing step is the constant `tau = 1/2`. **No eigendecomposition and no power iteration in the training path.** Ladder (2, 4, 6, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32) -> 9 telescoping atoms that sum to the target exactly.

**Decoder** — cross-field attention: each vertex spawns 4 field tokens (latent + learned per-field embedding), 2 attention blocks over the token axis with 4 heads, then a shared read-out MLP (64 hidden) -> one scalar per field.

## 4. Output and target

**Output** `(1, N, 4)` = `u_x, u_y, p, nu_t`, z-scored. Physical fields come from `pred * target_std + target_mean` then `redim_targets` (freestream re-dimensionalisation).

**Target** carries extra columns beyond the 4 fields where a case needs them: C_L weights + C_L_true + bias (3), peeled off by the trainer's `split_*` helpers so the stock collate is untouched.

## 5. Loss

```
L_field = 1.0 * MSE(non-wall vertices)
        + 1.0 * MSE(wall vertices)      # DISJOINT sets
          residuals divided by each sample's per-field std (floor 0.1)
L_band  = 0.5 * MSE(expert k band head, band k target)
L_bal   = 0.01 * (mean gate mass - 1/K)^2 * K
L_floor = 1.0 * sum_k relu(0.02 - share_k)^2   # one-sided
```

## 6. Training setup

| | |
|---|---|
| optimizer | adamw, weight decay 0.0001 |
| lr / schedule | 0.001 max, `onecycle` (pct_start 0.3, div 25.0, final_div 10000.0) |
| epochs / batch | 400 / 1 mesh |
| precision | bfloat16 autocast (the analyzer runs in fp32 outside autocast — sparse bmm has no bf16 CUDA kernel, and a supervision target should not carry autocast rounding) |
| checkpoints | every 20 epochs -> `runs/v57_gated_hodge_vef/` |
| per-epoch metrics | `runs/<case>/metrics.jsonl` + `metrics.csv` |

## 7. Data and split

| | |
|---|---|
| meshes | `/home/int/airfrans_data/graph_airfrans_data_v18_3` (~4.9k-vertex anisotropic-BL remeshes) |
| split | official AirfRANS **full 800/200**, `airfrans_official_split.json` |
| train augmentation | pool `__s0..__s7` (K=8), one random mesh per epoch |
| test | the 200 official test bases, fixed `__s0` mesh |
| geometry cache | `/home/int/airfrans_data/cache/v34_train_geo` |

## 8. Reproduce

```bash
# train (detached, ~33 h on one RTX 4090)
bash cases/v57_gated_hodge_vef/run_train_v57_gated_hodge_vef.sh

# 20-checkpoint sweep -> runs/<case>/eval_sweep/summary.txt
bash cases/v57_gated_hodge_vef/sweep_eval_v57_gated_hodge_vef.sh

# mesh-native lift at the best checkpoint
python cases/v57_gated_hodge_vef/eval_cl_native_v57_gated_hodge_vef.py --cfg_path cases/v57_gated_hodge_vef/airfrans_regression_v57_gated_hodge_vef_cfg.toml \
    --ckpt runs/v57_gated_hodge_vef/airfrans_hodgeformer-airfrans-v57_gated_hodge_vef_ckpt_<EP>.pth \
    --stats runs/v57_gated_hodge_vef/airfrans_norm_stats.npz --out runs/v57_gated_hodge_vef/eval_cl_ckpt<EP>

# qualitative figures (GT / prediction / |error| for all four fields)
python cases/v57_gated_hodge_vef/eval_airfrans_v57_gated_hodge_vef.py --cfg_path cases/v57_gated_hodge_vef/airfrans_regression_v57_gated_hodge_vef_cfg.toml \
    --ckpt runs/v57_gated_hodge_vef/..._ckpt_<EP>.pth --stats runs/v57_gated_hodge_vef/airfrans_norm_stats.npz \
    --out runs/v57_gated_hodge_vef/qual_ckpt<EP> --n_qual 8

# refresh the project tables
python tools/parse_sweeps.py && python tools/make_results_doc.py
```

**Determinism / provenance.** The split file, the pool and the geometry cache above pin the data exactly. Checkpoint selection for the reported row is the best rel-L2 over the 20-point sweep — note this selects on the TEST set (the baselines select on validation), which must be stated in any comparison.

